title: Maximum Number of Events That Can Be Attended II
summary: Given an array of events where each event is represented by [startDayi, endDayi, valuei], and an integer k representing the maximum number of events you can attend, determine the maximum sum of values you can achieve by attending non-overlapping events.
statement: Given an array of events where each event is represented by [startDayi, endDayi, valuei], and an integer k representing the maximum number of events you can attend, determine the maximum sum of values you can achieve by attending non-overlapping events. Each event you attend must be in its entirety, and you can only attend one event at a time. The end day of an event is inclusive, meaning you cannot attend two events that overlap on the same day.
constraints: Each event is [start,end,value], occupies both endpoint days, and may be attended whole.
Attend at most k nonoverlapping events to maximize total value.
hints: After sorting by start, selecting an event jumps to the first start strictly after its end.
Memoize the best value by event index and remaining slots.
Compare skipping with value+best(next_nonoverlap,left-1), locating next by upper-bound search.
Every feasible schedule either skips the current event or selects it and then lies wholly in the computed suffix.
editorial: Every feasible schedule either skips the current event or selects it and then lies wholly in the computed suffix.

tests.explanation: Events [1,2] and [3,4] do not overlap and total seven.
The value-ten event overlaps both others, so attending it alone is optimal.
